description: Terms the OPLS-AA 2024 BOSS files (J. Phys. Chem. B 128, 250 (2024), SI) lack for polymers of CAPS's library, each from the OPLS-AA paper that defines it, and atom types (caps_*) for environments the table has no number for, charged by OPLS-AA's own group increments; bench/ff/convert_boss_opls.py --supplement adds them only where the .sb has no entry (Jorgensen's files win). Units as the .sb: K in kcal/mol/A^2 or /rad^2 (E = K (x - x0)^2), r0 in A, theta0 in degrees.

bonds.source: E. K. Watkins, W. L. Jorgensen, J. Phys. Chem. A 105, 4118 (2001), Table 2
bonds.reason: the paper's perfluoroalkane carbons are class CT (the 2024 files' CF): a fluorinated carbon bonded to a hydrocarbon carbon is its CT-CT, 268.0 / 1.529 (the 2024 files' CF-CF)
a diene's central carbon (class C=) is the same sp2 carbon as an alkene CM; the files give C= its own terms only toward carbon and H, so the Cl takes CM's

angles.reason: the 2024 files' CF is the paper's CT

angles.source: W. L. Jorgensen, D. S. Maxwell, J. Tirado-Rives, J. Am. Chem. Soc. 118, 11225 (1996) (CT-CT-HC); Watkins & Jorgensen 2001
angles.reason: the perfluoroalkane paper has no H; with its CF = CT the bend is OPLS-AA's CT-CT-HC (the 2024 .sb's CT-CT-HC, 37.5 / 110.7)

angles.source: W. Damm, A. Frontera, J. Tirado-Rives, W. L. Jorgensen, J. Comput. Chem. 18, 1955 (1997), Table IV (CT-OS-CT, CT-OS-CO)
angles.reason: the paper's acetal carbon CO takes CT's bonded terms throughout (CT-OS-CO = CT-OS-CT, CT-CO-OS = CT-CT-OS); its C-O-C bend 60.0 / 109.5 (polyoxymethylene's O between two acetal carbons)
